annotation.title_clean: Moral and Ethical Scenarios for Educational Computer Games Based on the Robotic Futurology of Stanislaw Lem
annotation.title_en: Moral and Ethical Scenarios for Educational Computer Games Based on the Robotic Futurology of Stanislaw Lem
annotation.venue: Handbook of Research on Gamification Dynamics and User Experience Design (IGI Global)
annotation.summary_en: Book chapter proposing a method for building moral and ethical scenarios for educational computer games from Stanislaw Lem's robotic futurology stories, notably "Trurl's Machine". It formalizes plot conflicts into game design documents and a board-game prototype for forming students' values. It contains no robot or AI governance content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Develops a method for creating moral-ethical game scenarios from Lem's robotic stories
Formalizes moral conflicts in 'Trurl's Machine' into game mechanics and UML
Links directorial script with game design document
Rethinks a robot-themed board game prototype with pedagogical impact
